bounded_statement: The selected result in results/report.md was produced by feeding both measurements of every source item into a two-independent-samples t-test: the 12 distinct `k1`,`k2` source items each contribute one value to `left` (column `a`) and one value to `right` (column `b`), so each authorized independent unit enters the row-independent procedure twice and the reported df=22.0 asserts 24 mutually independent observations where only 12 independent units exist.

counterevidence_considered.description: No source item supplies more than one row: all 12 ordered `k1`,`k2` pairs are distinct, so the narrower reading of the issue class (a unit duplicated across rows) is not instantiated; the repeated entry occurs across columns within a row rather than across rows.

The `tag` column holds the constant value `shared` on every row, which could be read as an even coarser grouping (one item for all rows); task.md, however, fixes the unit key as the ordered `k1`,`k2` pair, so `tag` does not define the unit and is not the basis of this verdict.

evidence.description: task.md defines the ordered `k1`,`k2` pair as the source item, so both numeric columns on a given row belong to the same source item.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. Treat each distinct ordered `k1`,`k2` pair as one source item; rows carrying the same ordered pair originate from the same source item.

evidence.description: The workflow builds the two arms from columns `a` and `b` of the identical row list, so every staged row contributes exactly one entry to each arm.
evidence.observed_value: left and right iterate over the same `staged` sequence

source_refs.quoted_text:
staged = rows
left = [float(row["a"]) for row in staged]
right = [float(row["b"]) for row in staged]

evidence.description: The procedure applied is the independent-two-sample t-test, which treats all entries across both arms as independent observations.
The staged data contains 12 rows, i.e. 12 source items supplying 24 numeric measurements in total.

The selected report's degrees of freedom quantify the inflation: df=22.0 corresponds to n1+n2-2 = 24-2, i.e. 24 assumed-independent observations, versus 12 authorized independent units (a within-unit analysis of the same rows would carry 11 df).

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I first tried to falsify the verdict by looking for the most literal instantiation of the class and finding it absent: I checked every row key and confirmed all 12 ordered `k1`,`k2` pairs are unique, so no unit is repeated across rows, and I checked whether the workflow subsets, deduplicates or aggregates rows before testing (it does not; `staged = rows`). Under a reading of the class restricted to duplicated row keys, the verdict would flip to negative. I then tested whether the surviving reading could be explained away: could `a` and `b` legitimately come from different units? task.md states the ordered pair identifies the source item and each row carries exactly one such pair with both `a` and `b`, so the two arms are two measurements of the same 12 units, not 24 units. Could the report nonetheless reflect a unit-respecting analysis? No: df=22.0 is exactly n1+n2-2 for 12+12 entries, which is only correct if all 24 entries are independent, and `ttest_ind` offers no within-unit adjustment. I also considered the constant `tag` column as an alternative dependence story and rejected it as a basis, since the task fixes the unit key elsewhere; the verdict does not depend on `tag`. The remaining uncertainty is purely about how broadly the class name is scoped, not about the observed facts.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py constructs the two comparison arms as two columns of the same staged row set (`left` from `a`, `right` from `b`) and passes them to `scipy.stats.ttest_ind`, a procedure whose null distribution assumes every entry in both arms comes from a distinct independent unit. Because task.md designates each ordered `k1`,`k2` pair (i.e. each row here) as one source item, `a` and `b` on a row are two measurements of the same unit, and the within-unit pairing is discarded rather than modelled (no paired/within-unit test, no aggregation to one entry per unit).
